title: Triangulation and graded-split exact triangles in a DG derived category
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. The category $D(A,d)$, with the shifts induced by $M[k]^i=M^{i+k}$ and $d_{M[k]}=(-1)^kd_M$, is triangulated in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category], and the localization functor from the homotopy category is exact. If $0\to K\xrightarrow{u}L\xrightarrow{v}M\to0$ is a short exact sequence of right differential graded $A$-modules which splits as a sequence of graded right $A$-modules, there exists a morphism $\delta:M\to K[1]$ for which $K\xrightarrow{u}L\xrightarrow{v}M\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]$ is a distinguished triangle in $D(A,d)$. The first two arrows are the images of the specified inclusion and quotient maps. No compatibility of a graded splitting with the differentials is required.

source.place: Tag 09KJ, proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated; Tag 09K8, definition-distinguished-triangle, with Tag 09K6, lemma-triangle-independent-splittings; Tag 09KW, lemma-acyclic, and Tag 09KX, definition-unbounded-derived-category.

proof.text: Use $K_A$, the cone $C(f)=Y\oplus X[1]$ with $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and the signed cone triangle $T_f=(X,Y,C(f),f,i_f,-p_f)$. The Leibniz rule for its second coordinate has sign $(-1)^{n+1}$, which becomes $(-1)^n$ after applying $-d_X$; hence the unchanged right action makes it a DG module. A homotopy is an $A$-linear degree $-1$ map. Its composites with chain maps are homotopies, so quotienting maps defines an additive category with zero and finite direct sums. The shifts in the statement act on this category, sending $h$ to $(-1)^kh$ and having inverse $[-k]$. Declare triangles isomorphic to some $T_f$ distinguished. TR1 follows: every morphism has a chain-map representative; $C(1_X)$ contracts by $h(y,x)=(0,y)$, since $dh+hd=1$, giving the identity triangle. Isomorphism closure holds by definition.

source.place: Tag 09KJ, proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated, TR1 setup; Tag 09KF, lemma-the-same-up-to-isomorphisms (signed cone convention).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-cone-rotation] to a representative $f$ of a standard cone triangle. Both its rotation and its inverse rotation are isomorphic to standard cone triangles. Rotation and inverse rotation preserve triangle isomorphisms, so distinguishedness is preserved in both directions. This is TR2 with last arrow $-f[1]$, not $f[1]$.

source.place: Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, TR2; Tags 09KB and 09KC (the cone rotation input).

proof.text: For TR3, conjugate the two distinguished triangles to $T_f$ and $T_{f'}$. Represent the first two maps by chain maps $a:X\to X'$ and $b:Y\to Y'$. Their square commutes in $K_A$, so there is an $A$-linear degree $-1$ map $h$ with $bf-f'a=d_{Y'}h+hd_X$. The map $c(y,x)=(by+hx,ax)$ is a chain map: its upper-right chain-map equation is precisely that displayed homotopy equation, and its other equations are those for $a$ and $b$. Also $ci_f=i_{f'}b$ and $(-p_{f'})c=a[1](-p_f)$. This gives all three squares and, after undoing the triangle isomorphisms, proves TR3. Thus $K_A$ is pre-triangulated.

source.place: Tag 09KD, lemma-functorial-cone, matrix computation; Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, TR3.

proof.text: For TR4 choose composable chain representatives $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$. By [lem-sfb-dg-composite-cone-contraction], the triangle on the three cones with maps $\alpha(y,x)=(gy,x)$, $\beta(z,x)=(z,fx)$, $\gamma(z,y)=(-y,0)$ is isomorphic to $T_\alpha$ and hence distinguished. The octahedral squares are $\alpha i_f=i_{gf}g$, $p_{gf}\alpha=p_f$, $\beta i_{gf}=i_g$, and $p_g\beta=f[1]p_{gf}$. Its last arrow is exactly $\gamma=i_f[1](-p_g)$, as TR4 requires. For any prescribed distinguished triangles of these first arrows, TR3 completes the identity maps on their first two vertices to maps from the standard cones. Their third components are isomorphisms by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], which applies already to a pre-triangulated category. Conjugate $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ by these third isomorphisms. Every square and the last-arrow identity persist by substitution. This proves TR4 for the prescribed triangles, so $K_A$ is triangulated.

source.place: Tag 09KJ, proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated; Tag 09KI, lemma-two-split-injections, in cone coordinates. The arbitrary-cone reduction uses derived.tex Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle.

proof.text: Forget only to the underlying complexes of abelian groups. A homotopy acts trivially on cohomology because $(dh+hd)x=d(hx)$ for a cycle $x$; hence $H^n$ is defined on $K_A$. The cone fits into a degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to Y\xrightarrow{i_f}C(f)\xrightarrow{p_f}X[1]\to0$ of such complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. Its connecting homomorphism sends a cycle $x\in X^{n+1}$, lifted to $(0,x)$, to $f(x)$, since $d(0,x)=(fx,0)$. Exactness therefore says $C(f)$ is acyclic if and only if all $H^n(f)$ are isomorphisms: if the middle cohomology groups vanish the adjacent maps are bijective, and conversely bijectivity forces those middle groups to vanish. The same exact sequence shows that two acyclic vertices of a cone triangle force the third acyclic. Thus the full replete subcategory $\mathrm{Ac}$ of modules with all cohomology zero contains zero and is closed under shifts and distinguished triangles.

source.place: Tag 09KW, lemma-acyclic; equation-les in dga.tex, from homology.tex Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] to $K_A$ and $\mathrm{Ac}$. Its cone class $W$ is a multiplicative system admitting both fraction calculi and compatible with the triangulated structure. Step 5 identifies $W$ with precisely the quasi-isomorphisms, not a different class. Then [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] supplies the triangulation on $W^{-1}K_A=D(A,d)$ and exactness of $Q$. Its characterization of distinguished triangles says they are the triangles isomorphic to localized signed cone triangles, exactly the class in the statement. Sizes are handled in the universes fixed in [def-weil-size-convention]: finite direct sums, shifts and the cone constructions stay in the object universe; localization is taken in the larger universe allowed there. No small-index colimit or change of coefficient category is used.

proof.text: For the specified graded-split sequence choose degree-zero graded $A$-linear splittings $s:M\to L$, $\pi:L\to K$ with $vs=1$, $\pi u=1$, $u\pi+sv=1$, $\pi s=0$. Set $\delta=\pi d_Ls:M\to K[1]$. In coordinates $L=K\oplus M$ its differential is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_K&\delta\\0&d_M\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, so $d_L^2=0$ gives $d_K\delta+\delta d_M=0$. The Leibniz terms in $\delta(ma)$ cancel because $\pi s=0$, proving $\delta(ma)=\delta(m)a$; thus $\delta$ is a DG map to $K[1]$. Define $q:C(u)\to M$ by $q(l,k)=vl$, and $r:M\to C(u)$ by $r(m)=(sm,-\delta m)$. Direct multiplication gives $qr=1$ and $1-rq=dH+Hd$ for $H(l,k)=(0,\pi l)$. These maps and $H$ are $A$-linear. Finally $qi_u=v$ and $(-p_u)r=\delta$, so $(1_K,1_L,q)$ identifies $T_u$ with $(K,L,M,u,v,\delta)$ in $K_A$. Exactness of $Q$ from Step 6 makes its image distinguished. The first two maps are literally $Q(u)$ and $Q(v)$; no splitting was required to commute with $d_L$.
